assessment:
The catalog's wire behaviour is mostly documented correctly: endpoints, key format, S3 V1/V2 handling, settled semantics and lens evaluation match the code. The serious problems are architecture claims, fiction and rule breaches. (1) Five places say the catalog writes the `lens` table and prospector never reads it. In fact the catalog opens the database read-only, and prospector is the only writer and reads lenses constantly. (2) CATALOG-LENSES says closedness is never asked of the catalog, but the `settled` partitions API exists, and stocker and cold push rely on it. (3) CATALOG-UI.md describes lens-editor controls that do not exist: an instrument search, `every` labels, 'Both/Per instrument/Buckets', and refusals the catalog never makes. It credits prospector's /status facts to 'the catalog', claims an abort is passed on that the proxy drops, and is full of history. (4) UI.md and the _stub/ui README describe an architecture that was never built, env vars nothing reads, a `tb` target that does not exist, and two backends that are gone (BitMEX closed on 2026-09-23, digger retired). (5) Provider docs name their consumers, and settled, lens-through-contents and reporting each have two or three homes. (6) planning/CATALOG.md lists landed work, and ROADMAP links to an anchor and a file that do not exist. Two small code defects were found while verifying: the catalog-ui proxy does not pass aborts on, and `withdrawn` under a lens is the whole venue's. Both are bounded and fixing them is recommended over documenting the defect.

Recommended fresh-start structure: (a) docs/modules/CATALOG-API.md is the only reference for the wire contract (endpoints, params, fields, errors, wire meaning of settled), with no consumer narrative. (b) docs/modules/CATALOG-LENSES.md is the only home for what a lens is (definition, rules, refusals, resolution, members/rebuild, size, and how every endpoint narrows under a lens). Its consumer sections are cut. (c) docs/services/CATALOG.md is the implementation doc: read-only DB, forwarding to prospector (correct retry/502 semantics), the shared @tradebot/lenses package, how pages and lens walks are queried, what is cached, and the stillWanted check. It points to (a) and (b) instead of restating them. (d) docs/services/CATALOG-UI.md shrinks to about a third: proxy/token, routing, the three sections, Surveys polling and order-holding (attributed to prospector /status), and what the page derives itself. History, restated lens and /status semantics, control-by-control layout prose and dev instructions are cut. (e) docs/services/UI.md leaves the tech docs; any time-machine design worth keeping moves to docs/planning/UI.md. (f) READMEs become minimal: purpose, complete env table, commands, links. (g) planning/CATALOG.md loses its landed items; whether to rename or split it is an owner decision. Neighbouring docs that repeat the same errors must be fixed in the same change, so the contradictions do not survive there: ARCHIVES.md:33-35, the archives .env.example ('another machine'), PROSPECTOR.md:2045-2047 and the PROSPECTOR.md status table.

items.title: Docs say the catalog writes the lens table and prospector never reads it; prospector is the only writer
items.problem: CATALOG-LENSES.md:13-16 says 'the catalog writes the `lens` table (the one table it writes) and prospector never reads it'. The same doc at :148-149, CATALOG.md:11-23 and the code all say prospector writes both tables. The false version is repeated in ARCHIVES.md:33-35 ('the catalog writes the `lens` table and nothing else'), the compose comment ('It writes only lenses'), the config.ts docblock ('to read it and to store lenses') and the types.ts:19 comment. An engineer who follows it would write through a read-only connection.
items.evidence: services/catalog/src/database.ts:26-27 has `new DatabaseSync(path, { readOnly: true })`, and there is no INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE in services/catalog/src. api/lenses.ts forwards POST/PUT/DELETE through `stored()` to prospector's `send()`, and its docblock says 'A lens is stored by prospector, never here'. Prospector writes lenses with putLens/editLens/dropLens (prospector/src/api/lenses.ts:37,53,69). It also reads them: `catchUp(db, lens, STEP)` (prospector/src/lenses.ts:53) and `admit(db, lenses(db), id)` (prospector/src/catalog/cache/partitions.ts:152).
items.fix:
1. CATALOG-LENSES.md:13-16: replace the paragraph with 'Lenses are defined, checked and read through the catalog's API; prospector, the database's only writer, stores them and keeps `lens_member` current (see CATALOG.md#one-database-one-writer).' Keep only one of this sentence and the :148-149 paragraph. Do not say prospector never reads lenses.
2. ARCHIVES.md:33-35: replace with 'A lens is a consumer's choice of what to read, so it is defined and checked through the catalog; prospector stores it like every other row, and the catalog opens the database read-only.' Add storing lenses to prospector's private API list at :29-30.
3. services/catalog/docker/compose.yml:4-6: change the comment to 'It opens the database read-only and writes nothing; lens writes and download reports are forwarded to prospector, which owns every row.'
4. services/catalog/src/config.ts:9-10: change to 'this service opens the same file read-only'.
5. services/catalog/src/types.ts:19: change to 'The catalog database prospector keeps, opened here read-only.' Rebuild so dist follows.
6. Check: `grep -rn "store lenses\|writes only lenses\|catalog writes" --include='*.md' --include='*.ts' --include='*.yml' . | grep -v node_modules | grep -v dist` returns nothing.
items.tests: None (docs and comments only). Run tsc for the comment edits.
items.verifier_notes: Both verifiers confirmed at high severity. The first verifier also found types.ts:19. The second asked that ARCHIVES.md's private-API list be extended so its two paragraphs agree.

items.title: CATALOG-LENSES 'Who reads through one' is wrong about readiness, and provider docs name their consumers
items.problem:
CATALOG-LENSES.md:204-207 says readiness is reached once every file a lens lists is on disk, and that whether a month is closed 'is never asked of the catalog'. The catalog serves `settled` and `settled-before` on /venues/:venue/partitions, and stocker and cold push decide readiness with them. The surrounding section and several other passages also explain the provider by its consumers, against CLAUDE.md's dependency rule:
- CATALOG-LENSES.md:8-9 ('hauler downloads through one, stocker builds through one, cold storage decides through one').
- :196-210: downloader deployments, stocker, cold storage and PROSPECTOR_VENUES.
- CATALOG-API.md:188-190 ('This is what a downloader walks').
- CATALOG-API.md:299-305: the downloader re-lists and re-reports, plus hauler's adoption, which HAULER.md:192 already owns.
- The catalog-ui README:25-26 ('such as the one hauler downloads').
items.evidence: partitions.ts:66-102 implements `settledEdge`. stocker/src/catalog.ts sends `downloaded=true` and `'settled': 'true'`. COLD-PUSH.md:16-21 asks the partitions endpoint with `downloaded=true` and `settled`. HAULER.md:192 has '### Adopting an archive that already exists'.
items.fix:
CATALOG-LENSES.md:
- :8-9 becomes 'It is how a consumer says what it wants without the catalog changing. The endpoints are in CATALOG-API.md; the editor is in CATALOG-UI.md.'
- Delete the readiness paragraph :204-207 outright.
- Replace the rest of :196-210 with one provider-side statement under 'Reading through a lens': '**Pending is the file's, not the lens's.** A file reported downloaded through any lens is no longer pending through any other.' Keep 'a lens never scopes collection' (already said on the catalog's terms) and drop the PROSPECTOR_VENUES sentence.
- Move the 'disjoint lens per downloader' advice to HAULER.md, and readiness-against-a-complete-lens to STOCKER.md and the cold docs, if they do not already say it.
CATALOG-API.md:
- Add one line to the partitions section: 'A lens narrows which partitions are listed; `settled` and `downloaded` say whether each is complete enough to act on.'
- :188-190 becomes 'The catalog as one storage bucket: every venue's files, in S3's shape, each keyed by what the file *is*. A report names files by the same key.'
- :299-305 becomes 'A report is prospector's to settle: the catalog resolves each key to its file and forwards it. Where prospector does not answer or refuses, the report is a `502` and nothing was recorded. Settling the same report twice is harmless, so it can simply be sent again.' Drop the adoption sentence.
catalog-ui README: drop 'such as the one hauler downloads' (done in DCAT-07's README rewrite).
items.verifier_notes: Merges reviewer F3 (high) and F10 (medium). The first verifier lowered F3 to medium: CATALOG-API and the consumer docs carry the correct behaviour, and nothing executes this paragraph. It also rejected deleting the section wholesale, because the 'pending is per file' fact is the catalog's own behaviour and must survive.

items.title: catalog-ui proxy does not pass the browser's abort on, so the documented cancellation never takes effect
items.problem: CATALOG-UI.md:361-363 says leaving a view aborts the request in flight and 'the catalog does not start work for a client that has gone'. CATALOG.md:143-147 says the same of an editor that has moved on. The browser does abort its fetch to catalog-ui, but `forward()` calls `fetch(url, ...)` with no AbortSignal and never watches for the client leaving. The upstream connection stays open, the catalog's `stillWanted` sees `req.socket.destroyed === false`, and the work runs anyway. The only editor that exists reaches the catalog through this proxy.
items.evidence: routes.ts forward(): `const answer = await fetch(url, { method: req.method, headers: {...}, ...body })`, with no `signal` and no close listener. api/index.ts stillWanted: `if (req.socket.destroyed) return; next();`.
items.tests: In catalog-ui tests: start a stub upstream that holds its answer, for example for 2 s. Make a GET through forward, then destroy the client socket. Assert that the upstream request's socket closes, or its 'close' event fires, before the delay ends, and that no 502 or warn is logged. A second test checks that a POST is not aborted when the client leaves.
items.verifier_notes: The verifier confirmed the defect and corrected the reviewer's fix (use res.on('close') with writableFinished, GET/HEAD only).

items.title: Under a lens, /venues reports the whole venue's `withdrawn`, and `series` always reads n/n
items.problem: CATALOG-API.md:80 says 'Under a lens every figure is the lens's'. In venueContents the lensed branch spreads `...row` from venueTotals and overrides files, bytes, pending, pendingBytes and the months, but not `withdrawn`, so `withdrawn` stays the venue's. `series` becomes `{ withFiles: inside, total: inside }`, so the pair always reads n/n under a lens.
items.evidence: contents.ts:63-73 returns `{ ...row, firstMonth, lastMonth, files, bytes, pending, pendingBytes, series: { withFiles: inside, total: inside }, hosts }` with no `withdrawn`. lensFigures does not select withdrawn. venueTotals has `COALESCE(SUM(m.withdrawn),0) AS withdrawn` over the whole venue. Impact is limited: catalog-ui renders withFiles/total only in Surveys, which sends no lens.
items.fix: Code: in services/catalog/src/lenses/figures.ts add `COALESCE(SUM(q.withdrawn), 0) AS withdrawn`, add `withdrawn: number` to LensVenueFigures in types.ts, and set `withdrawn: figures.withdrawn` in contents.ts:63-73. savedLensSize is unchanged. Docs: in CATALOG-LENSES.md#reading-through-a-lens (the single home, see DCAT-16), state that under a lens every figure including `withdrawn` is the lens's, and that `series` counts the series dated inside the lens, so `withFiles` equals `total`. CATALOG-API.md:80 points there.
items.tests: In the catalog contents tests, build a venue with a withdrawn file in a partition outside a lens and none inside it. Assert that GET /venues with x-catalog-lens returns withdrawn 0 and series.withFiles === series.total, and that GET /venues without the lens returns withdrawn 1.
items.verifier_notes: Confirmed medium. The fix chosen is the code fix plus a doc clarification for series.

items.title: UI.md and the _stub/ui README describe an unbuilt architecture, unread env vars and gone backends
items.problem:
UI.md:
- It is a design plan written as fact. src/hooks/, LiveClient/ReplayClient, src/data/channels/*, useChannel, useCandles and TimeControlProvider do not exist.
- Types are said to live in `shared/types`; the stub uses src/types.ts.
- 'Current State (as of April 2026)' says providers do not exist, but DataProvider and EnvProvider do.

The _stub/ui README:

Compose sets UI_REPLAY_HOST, which vite.config.ts never reads (it reads UI_DIGGER_HOST), and the EnvSwitcher/envs docblocks repeat the wrong name. Both backends are gone: BitMEX closed on 2026-09-23 and digger is retired (DATA_PIPELINE.md:152-157).

items.fix:
1. Remove docs/services/UI.md from the tech docs. Move whatever replay/time-machine design is worth keeping to docs/planning/UI.md, written as an explicit plan with no 'current state' section and no claims about existing files. Delete it outright if the owner does not want it (see owner question).
2. Rewrite services/_stub/ui/README.md in present tense:
- What it is: a BitMEX-era React/Vite dashboard kept as a stub, not wired into any module. BitMEX closed on 2026-09-23 and its replay backend (digger) is retired.
- What exists: a Vite dev server only, routing on `/:symbol`, react-grid-layout with 12 columns persisted to localStorage, most widgets on mockData.ts.
- An env table with what vite.config.ts and compose actually read: UI_PORT (3000), UI_REST_PROXY (default http://proxy, which no module provides), UI_DIGGER_HOST (empty disables Replay), UI_DIGGER_WS_PORT (8180), UI_DIGGER_REST_PORT (3101), UI_DIGGER_CONTROL_PORT (8280).
- Run with `pnpm --filter @tradebot/ui dev`.
- Drop the tb block and the UI.md link, or point the link at the planning doc.
3. Rename UI_REPLAY_HOST to UI_DIGGER_HOST in docker/compose.yml:19-21, EnvSwitcher.tsx:4 and envs.ts:5, or delete the replay wiring.
items.tests: None (docs and dev config). Optionally run `pnpm --filter @tradebot/ui build` or tsc after the docblock edits.

items.title: CATALOG-UI and the catalog-ui README claim refusals and pre-save sizing the catalog does not do
items.problem: CATALOG-UI.md:324-329 lists two refusals 'about meaning': a venue whose rules include nothing, and an empty list in a dimension. `problemsWith` refuses neither, and CATALOG-LENSES.md:106-109 says what a rule matches is never weighed. The catalog-ui README:26-28 says a lens is 'sized before it is saved, and refused where it claims more than a venue publishes'. Both halves are false: only the saved lens is sized, and nothing compares a rule with what a venue publishes.
items.evidence: draft.ts faultsIn() checks only unknown venue, grain, bundle, exclude+prefer, `yyyymm` bounds and from>to. rules.ts `named(values, one)` returns `values.includes(one)`, so `[]` silently matches nothing. Lenses.tsx:252 requests only `/lenses/${slug}/size`. CATALOG-UI.md:332 itself says 'A draft is never sized'.
items.fix: CATALOG-UI.md:324-329: '**The catalog decides what can be stored.** A confirm it refuses comes back with its problems, shown on the rule, which stays a draft (what is refused: CATALOG-LENSES#what-is-refused).' Drop the two 'meaning' cases. If wanted, add to CATALOG-LENSES (not here) that a venue including nothing, or an empty list, is stored as written and lets nothing through. In services/catalog-ui/README.md:25-28, replace the lenses bullet with '**lenses**: named slices of the catalog, edited as rules per venue and under All venues; a saved lens shows its exact size and how much of it is downloaded.'
items.verifier_notes: Confirmed medium.

items.title: CATALOG-UI credits prospector's /status facts to 'the catalog' and to 'this process'
items.problem: Surveys polls prospector's /status, but the Surveys text calls the source 'the catalog' throughout (:119, 130, 143, 158, 173, 241, 276). In this doc that means the catalog service. :157-161 says only 'this process' (catalog-ui) can tell whether a loop is alive. That text was carried over from prospector's point of view: `surveying` is prospector's field, and catalog-ui only derives the word `stalled` from it. The Surveys.tsx:555-561 docblock repeats the error. The every-host rule for `completedEver` is stated only here, while PROSPECTOR.md owns /status.
items.evidence: web/api.ts: `prospector = (path) => ask('/api/prospector'+path)`. Surveys polls `prospector('/status')`. Surveys.tsx State: `if (working && ! of.surveying) return <Badge color="red">stalled</Badge>`. PROSPECTOR.md:2037 says '`surveying` whether **this process** has a loop alive'. collector.ts:260 has `ids.every(id => everCompleted(db, id))`.
items.fix:
1. Replace 'the catalog' with 'prospector' wherever the Surveys section means the source of /status: :119, :130, :143, :158, :173, :241 ('no separate resume verb') and :276.
2. Rewrite :157-161 as '`stalled` is this page's word for a venue prospector reports as `walking` or `updating` with `surveying: false`: work outstanding, and no loop of prospector's doing it.' Make the same correction in the Surveys.tsx:555-561 docblock.
3. Move the every-host rule into PROSPECTOR.md's Status table: '`completedEver` | whether a pass has ever finished on every one of the venue's hosts'.
4. Then cut CATALOG-UI.md:219-223 to one sentence saying the badge uses the same field. Keep :210-217, which is the consumer's reason for its choice and belongs here per CLAUDE.md.

items.title: Forwarding to prospector: retry count, 502 meaning and lens-write retries are misdescribed
items.problem: CATALOG.md:32 says 'tried again, three times'. ATTEMPTS = 3 means three attempts in all, which is two retries. A non-2xx answer from prospector throws Refused, is not retried, and is answered with 502 too, so a 502 also means prospector refused. Lens writes go through the same retry loop, which no doc mentions. A create retried after a dropped connection can come back 409.
items.evidence: reports.ts: `if (! answer.ok) throw new Refused(...)` and `if (err instanceof Refused || attempt >= ATTEMPTS) throw err;`. api/reports.ts answers every throw with 502 'ServiceUnavailable'. prospector.ts has the same loop for lens writes.
items.fix: CATALOG.md:32-35 becomes 'A connection prospector drops is retried, up to three attempts in all, because it closes idle keep-alive connections ... and settling twice is harmless. Where prospector still does not answer, or answers with an error, the report is a `502`; ...' After :23 add 'A dropped connection is retried the same way; where the first attempt was stored before the connection went, the retry is answered as a second write would be (a create, `409`).' CATALOG-API.md:297/:300 becomes '`502` where prospector does not answer or refuses the report'. Change the code comments at reports.ts:76 and prospector.ts:11 to 'up to three attempts'.
items.verifier_notes: Confirmed low. The 409-on-retry case is narrow (the connection has to drop after prospector processed the write), so it gets one clause, not a section.

items.title: CATALOG-API error table and S3-error claim are incomplete
items.problem: The listing is said to answer errors 'in S3's shape, errors included', but 401 (requireToken), 413 (body parser) and 500 (onError) answer `{ "error" }` JSON on /listings too. The Errors table gives 502 only for reports, but lens writes also answer 502. The table also lacks 400 for an unsound slug and for an unknown `bundle`, and 422 for `NoSuchPartition`.

items.title: Small inaccuracies in CATALOG-API's listing, contents and key-grammar sections
items.problem:

- :29-31 says the variant is answered as an object, but partitions, lens options and the market row's `variants` carry the stored string.

items.evidence: api/listings.ts:13 says 'Three filters'. api/contents.ts:62-66 shows the partitions params. partitions.ts:52 has `variant: row.variant`. bitget.ts:64 has `FIRST_PART = '001'`. gate.ts:101/111 use an epoch part. lenses/scope.ts:9-15 reads lens_member.
items.fix:
- 'Three filters S3 does not have'. - :166 becomes 'Markets, shapes and symbols take the filters `market`, `dataset`, `variant` and `grain`; partitions takes its own, below.' - :29-31: shapes answer the variant as an object; the market row's `variants`, partitions and lens options carry the stored string (`incremental,500`), since that is what a filter or rule names. - In the key grammar (:205-206, :221, :228), write `.part

`, where P is the part as the venue writes it: a two-digit hour for gate's hourly files, a three-digit piece for bitget, an epoch for gate's slices. - :80-81 becomes 'Under a lens every figure is the lens's, read from its `lens_member` rows; those are held until the lens is saved again or admits a partition.' Do not restate any seconds figure.

items.title: Catalog caches are undocumented, so contents and lens options can be minutes old
items.problem:
Three things are held between requests and no doc says so:
- Venue series for 60 s, so markets, shapes, symbols and lens-filtered contents trail a survey by up to a minute.
- Lens options for 5 min, so a new dataset is missing from the editor's pick lists.
- Lens scopes until the lens changes or admits a partition.
CATALOG-API.md:183 says contents 'cost nothing to ask', which is misleading.
items.evidence: queries.ts has `const SERIES_MS = 60_000;`. draft.ts has `const OPTIONS_MS = 5 * 60_000;`. scope.ts has the SCOPES map keyed on updatedAt/partitions_through.
items.fix: Add a short 'What is held between requests' paragraph under Contents in CATALOG.md: a venue's series for a minute; a lens's scope until it is saved again or admits a partition; partitions, settled state and listing pages are never held. State the 5-minute lens-options hold in the @tradebot/lenses home (CATALOG-LENSES.md, or shared/lenses' README), with a one-line mention in CATALOG.md. CATALOG-API.md:181-183: 'so it is cheap to ask; the answer can be up to a minute behind prospector'.
items.verifier_notes: Confirmed and recalibrated from medium to low: the answers are stale, not wrong.

items.title: Settled, lens-filtered contents, reporting and lens rule semantics each have several homes
items.problem:
This breaks the 'each subject has one home' rule. The texts agree today, so this is a drift risk rather than a contradiction. The clearest duplicates:
- CATALOG-API.md:299-309 restates how prospector rules on a report, which PROSPECTOR.md owns.
- CATALOG-UI.md restates lens rule semantics that CATALOG-LENSES owns.
- CATALOG-UI.md describes localStorage drafts twice (:335-338 and :354-359).
- CATALOG.md:83-85 repeats the caller-facing 'not a promise' paragraph on settled.
items.evidence: The cited line ranges.
items.fix:
- Settled: CATALOG-API.md's partitions section owns what a caller can rely on. CATALOG.md drops :83-85 for a pointer, and keeps the implementation (the open run read by venue, one comparison, read once per request, SETTLE_DAYS).
- Lens effects on endpoints: CATALOG-LENSES#reading-through-a-lens is the single home. CATALOG-API.md:80-82 points there. Leave CATALOG.md:58-61 as is, since it is the implementation note (one query on lens_member).
- Reporting: CATALOG-API.md:307-309 is replaced with 'How prospector rules on a failure or a mismatch is in PROSPECTOR.md#reports.'
- CATALOG-UI: replace the semantics at :287-290 and :345-347 with one line pointing to CATALOG-LENSES.md#the-definition, keeping only what the editor shows (every venue's block, All/Any for an absent dimension, per DCAT-06). Merge :335-338 and :354-359 into one paragraph: drafts are kept per lens in localStorage, tagged with the version they were written from, so a reload keeps them, a lens saved elsewhere replaces them, and 'Reload as saved' drops them.
items.verifier_notes: The verifier lowered this from medium to low, since no contradiction was found. Conflict resolved: the verifier's refined fix said to keep '`every` for an absent dimension', but DCAT-06 shows no `every` label exists, so All/Any is used.

items.title: Wrong catalog-ui build and dev instructions, stated in two places
items.problem: The README's build comment omits `tsc -p web`. CATALOG-UI.md:375-376 says `dev` runs Vite against the built server 'exactly as in the container'. In fact Vite only proxies /api to localhost:8080, and nothing starts that server. CATALOG_API defaults to http://catalog:8080, and PROSPECTOR_API is the constant http://prospector:8080, so the Surveys tab cannot work outside the module network. The container publishes 9020, not 8080. Dev setup is duplicated, and the vite.config.ts docblock overstates it too.
items.evidence: package.json has `"build": "tsc -p web && vite build && tsc -b"` and `"dev": "vite"`. vite.config.ts has `proxy: { '/api': 'http://localhost:8080' }`. compose has `${CATALOG_UI_PORT:-9020}:8080`.
items.fix: README.md:40: `# tsc -p web && vite build && tsc -b`. README.md:41-42: '`dev` serves the page with Vite and proxies `/api` to a catalog-ui server on :8080, which you start yourself (`CATALOG_API=http://localhost:<catalog port> pnpm --filter @tradebot/catalog-ui start` after a build); the Surveys tab needs prospector's module network.' Delete CATALOG-UI.md:375-376 so the README is the one home. Soften the vite.config.ts docblock to say the page talks to its own origin, as it does in the container.
items.verifier_notes: Confirmed low.

items.title: Catalog README restates endpoints incompletely and omits CATALOG_DB
items.problem: The README lists endpoints, although CATALOG-API.md says it is the only home for them, and the list omits /venues/:venue/partitions. The env table omits CATALOG_DB, the database path override that config.ts reads. LOG_LEVEL, NODE_ENV and TZ, which compose passes, are undocumented too.
items.evidence: config.ts has `dbPath: process.env['CATALOG_DB'] ?? CATALOG_DB`. `grep -rn CATALOG_DB --include=*.md` finds nothing.
items.fix: Replace the endpoint block with 'It serves venue contents, the bucket listing and lenses; every endpoint is in CATALOG-API.md.' Add the row `CATALOG_DB` | `/data/catalog/catalog.db` | path of the database inside the process; compose leaves it at the `CATALOG_DIR` mount, and setting it runs the service against another file (e.g. outside compose). Optionally note that compose passes LOG_LEVEL (info), NODE_ENV and TZ (UTC) through.
items.verifier_notes: Confirmed low.

items.title: shared/lenses and catalog docblocks contradict the code (rule order, bound format, resolve answer)
items.problem:
- The LensRule docblock says rules apply in order, read top to bottom, and that a list opening with exclude sees nothing. spansFor is order-free.
- types.ts:133 says bounds are `yyyymmdd`, but they are `yyyymm`.
- store.ts:156 is history ('Lenses written before a bound was a month').
- api/lenses.ts:134 says resolve answers 'how many series', but it answers slices, partitions and spans.
items.evidence: rules.ts spansFor says 'Order-free. The includes are one set and the excludes another'. draft.ts:167-170 says 'Bounds are written yyyymm'. draft.ts:74-83 resolvedSummary.
items.fix:
- LensRule (:85-91): 'One rule. A lens lets through what any of its includes match, less what any of its excludes match; where a rule sits never changes the result, and an exclude always wins over an include it overlaps (see `spansFor`).' Keep the 'states only what it constrains' paragraph and drop the 'considered and rejected' paragraph (:97-101).
- types.ts:133: 'Inclusive `yyyymm` bounds on the period a file covers; absent is open.'
- store.ts:156-161: 'Bounds as months: any longer stamp is truncated to its month, which is how a bound is compared everywhere.'
- api/lenses.ts:134: 'by venue: how many slices and partitions, and the month spans its rules bound them to.'
